clue.text: Testimony of master's taking precedence

indicators.note: going first, so the master's word comes before the little word of

parts.note: a master of a craft is a pro, an expert professional
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer weighs evidence in which the master's word outranks everyone else's.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony is evidence offered to establish a fact, which is what proof means in a court.

clue.text: Steep charge placed on official staff

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece set on another follows it, so the charge comes after the staff

parts.note: a mace is the ceremonial staff carried before an official
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A steep fee is imposed on the staff of some public office.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something in liquid until it softens is to macerate it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Presbyter announces staff member with gravitas

parts.note: a presbyter is an elder of a church
to announce is to state, so announces gives states
to staff a post is to man it

explanation.surface: A church official proclaims a new and serious-minded recruit to the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announces' looks like a sound signal, but it simply means STATES, and 'staff' is a verb, MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder statesman is a senior, respected figure whose weight and experience lend authority, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Poor chairwoman's cut with small instrument

indicators.note: poor here means in a bad state, so the remaining letters are knocked into a new order
the chairwoman's letters are cut by taking one away

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A struggling chairwoman finds her budget slashed along with a small musical outlay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' with 'with' removes W (an abbreviation for with) from CHAIRWOMAN; 'Poor' then rearranges CHAIROMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica, or mouth organ, is a small hand-held wind instrument.

clue.text: Flock on the move hide round back of copse

indicators.note: the skin goes round, enclosing the letter that follows

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A bird-watcher's hide stands near a small wood as birds pass over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flock' looks like sheep, but a skein is a flight of wild geese.
explanation.definitionFit: Skein is the collective noun for wild geese in flight, a flock moving through the air.

clue.text: Like ears, primarily of barley, brought in behind time

indicators.note: the picked letters are brought inside the other piece

parts.note: behind time means late

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A farmer's barley is gathered late, its ears ripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ears' suggests heads of grain to fit barley, but the definition is about the lobes of the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobate means having lobes, and the human ear is noted for its lobe.

clue.text: Understand the heart of every piece when playing

indicators.note: playing suggests letters moving about, so the pieces are rearranged
the heart of a word is everything inside its outer letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician grasps the core of each composition as it is performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the heart of' takes VER from EVERY; 'when playing' rearranges VER with PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive something is to grasp it with the mind, a verb synonym for understand.

clue.text: Close to being plump, not allowed to fly

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: plump means rounded, full in figure

explanation.surface: An overweight passenger is denied boarding for being nearly too plump.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft or pilot that is grounded is forbidden to take to the air.

clue.text: Ancient Mariner's main trouble?

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open ocean
to dog is to trouble or harass persistently

explanation.surface: A question about what plagued Coleridge's old sailor on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner is Coleridge's poem; here the phrase just means an old sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea dog is a veteran sailor, which is what an ancient mariner is.

clue.text: What's in notes put back in bundle

indicators.note: put back means the whole is turned so it reads from the other end
the query goes inside the notes

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale, so notes gives fas
eh? is a way of asking what

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is in a bundle of papers being filed away again.
explanation.walkthrough: FAS, the plural of the sol-fa note fa, is a rare but valid spelling; 'put back' turns the whole assembly, not just the notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle, of corn stalks or of papers tied together.

clue.text: Engineers attentive to detail removing part forming network

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: removing means the named letters are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: particular means fussy, attentive to detail
par is taken as a shortening of part

explanation.surface: Fussy engineers are dismantling a component that forms part of a network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes PAR out of PARTICULAR, leaving TICULAR; bloggers felt part for PAR was a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticular means net-like or forming a network, from the Latin for a little net.

clue.text: More than satisfy past company members worried about Englishman's case

parts.note: over means finished, past

indicators.note: the members and worried go about the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters

parts.note: ate, as in what's eating you, means worried

explanation.surface: Former directors fretting over an Englishman's legal case try too hard to make amends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' as ATE comes from 'what's eating you?'; 'case' means the outer letters of the word, a common crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcompensate is to make amends or adjust to excess, going beyond merely satisfying a claim.

clue.text: Prisoner put under obligation briefly

parts.note: to inter is to bury, putting a body under the ground

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a need is a necessity or obligation

explanation.surface: A captive is held under a duty for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put under' is not about debt: it means bury, INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is someone confined, especially in wartime, so a kind of prisoner.

clue.text: Quickly passed info back, dropping first part

indicators.note: back means the shortened word is read in reverse
the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: news is information

explanation.surface: Someone quickly relayed some information, leaving out the opening section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quickly passed' is the definition, so 'passed info back' is not one phrase; 'dropping first' applies to the info before 'back' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swept describes moving swiftly past, as a car that swept by went quickly.

clue.text: Dreadful gossip to help dedicated social scientist

indicators.note: dreadful means in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Malicious gossip is used to assist a committed academic.
explanation.definitionFit: A psephologist studies elections and voting patterns, a branch of political and social science.

clue.text: Arrange company booking

definitions.meaning: to ... things is to arrange them in sequence
a religious ... is a company of monks or nuns
placing an ... is making a booking for goods or a table

explanation.definitionFit: Order works as a verb for arranging, a noun for a fraternity, and a noun for a reservation.

clue.text: Unremembered ex-president briefly arrested in US

indicators.note: briefly means the name is cut short by a letter

parts.note: Gerald Ford was a US president
got means arrested, and Americans say gotten for the past participle

explanation.surface: A former president, held for a short time in America, is no longer remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has slipped from memory, so it is unremembered.

clue.text: Array of sound from springtime is deceptive

indicators.note: the pieces are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: May is springtime and tricks means is deceptive

explanation.surface: Spring weather can fool you with its pleasant sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: May tricks, said aloud, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers or elements in rows and columns.

clue.text: Countryman and commander recalled short meeting on river

parts.note: CO is commanding officer

indicators.note: recalled, called back, means the shortened word is read backwards
short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a regatta is a boat-racing meeting on a river

explanation.surface: A rural man and his commanding officer cut short their gathering by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims REGATTA to REGATT, and 'recalled' turns it to TTAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottager is a person living in a country cottage, a rural dweller.

clue.text: Society's overwhelmed by mounting box files

indicators.note: the letter is overwhelmed, swallowed up, by the surrounding piece
mounting in a down answer means reading upwards

parts.note: to spar is to box
S is short for Society

explanation.surface: A society is buried under a growing pile of boxed documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns SPAR into RAPS, which takes S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasps are coarse files, and to rasp is to file, so files works as noun or verb.

clue.text: A blow for business?

parts.note: reads as a setback for commerce but means a wind that helped merchant sailing ships

explanation.definitionFit: Trade winds are steady easterlies once relied on by merchant ships, so a breeze that served commerce.

clue.text: German turned out drawers, maybe

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German emptied out a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like the signal, but it is part of the letters; 'out' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawers, or knickers, are an example of an item of underwear.

clue.text: Changing sides, chap still neither won nor lost

indicators.note: left is swapped for right, so the L becomes R

parts.note: bloke is British slang for a chap
still and even both mean level, calm

explanation.surface: A man who switched teams still ended up with no gain or loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To break even is to finish with no profit or loss overall.

clue.text: Cartel every so often picks up bent ways

indicators.note: every so often means take letters at regular intervals

parts.note: picks up, as a dog does, means scents

explanation.surface: A cartel periodically detects crooked routes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' suggests corruption, but here means curved; crescents are curved streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent is a street built in a curved arc, a common British road name.

clue.text: Press in particular supporting Vandyke, say

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits below

parts.note: a Vandyke is a pointed style of beard
one's own is particular to oneself

explanation.surface: The newspapers seem especially keen on a painter's fashionable beard.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear down is to press or push hard, as in childbirth or on an opponent.

clue.text: Basic pressure for British in firm

indicators.note: one letter stands in for another

parts.note: stable means firm and steady
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Fundamental strain on a British company.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic item, and the adjective means main or chief.

clue.text: Prickly shrub an unethical form of covering, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means heard rather than read

parts.note: furs are a garment many see as unethical

explanation.surface: A thorny plant is said to be an immoral garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Furze, also called gorse, is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub.

clue.text: Skip most of pages

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: leaves of a book are its pages

explanation.surface: Skip most of the pages in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to skip it, a verb synonym.
